Expectation1: Attending children's school events and activities
Situation1: Children are about to finish school, and the mother should pick them up
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was nearly midnight when my phone buzzed, jolting me from a light sleep. I saw my friend’s name on the screen, and when I answered, her voice was trembling, thick with tears. She could barely get the words out—her family had just received terrible news, and she needed someone to talk to, someone to listen. I sat up, heart pounding, trying to offer comfort, but my mind kept drifting to the clock. In just a few hours, I needed to be up, dressed, and ready to pick up my kids from school. It was their last day, and they’d been so excited for me to be there, to see their faces as they ran out of the building, searching for me in the crowd. My friend’s pain was raw and immediate, and I wanted to be the support she needed, but the thought of letting my children down gnawed at me. I felt torn, caught between the needs of someone I loved and the promises I’d made to my children, unsure how to be both the mother and the friend they each deserved.
